title: The Last Judgment
shows: The whole altar-wall fresco: Christ in judgment, the saints, the trumpeting angels, the dead rising at left and Charon's boat and Minos at the lower right.

title: The Last Judgment (detail: Charon's boat, crop of the full fresco)
shows: Charon raising his oar to drive the damned out of his boat; a soul clutches his face in terror (cropped by us from the full-wall image; the altar crucifix and candles intrude at lower left).
note: Cropped by us from the full-wall image of the Commons file.

title: The Last Judgment (detail: Charon the ferryman)
shows: Older, darker (pre-restoration) reproduction of Charon swinging his oar over the boatload of damned souls.

title: The Last Judgment (detail: Minos)
shows: Minos, judge of the underworld, with ass's ears and a serpent coiled around him, surrounded by demons.

title: Landscape with Charon Crossing the Styx
shows: Charon rows a soul across a broad river between Paradise (left) and the burning mouth of Hell guarded by Cerberus (right).

title: The Damned (Cappella di San Brizio)
location: Cappella di San Brizio, Orvieto Cathedral
shows: Winged demons seize and torment a heaving mass of naked damned souls while armoured archangels look on.

title: Resurrection of the Flesh (detail)
location: Cappella di San Brizio, Orvieto Cathedral
shows: Under a trumpeting angel, the dead climb out of the earth and regain their bodies beside skeletons.

title: Charon's Boat (Gallery ceiling, Palazzo Medici-Riccardi)
shows: Charon poles his boat as souls clamber aboard, with Death wielding a scythe, three-headed Cerberus on the rocks, and Night spreading her starry mantle above.

title: White-ground lekythos: Charon receiving Hermes and a dead woman
author: ArchaiOptix
shows: Athenian funerary oil-flask painted with Charon in his pointed cap, standing in his boat with his punt pole (this view shows Charon only).

title: Mercury (Loggia di Psiche spandrel)
location: Loggia di Psiche, Villa Farnesina, Rome
shows: Winged-hatted Mercury flies down with his trumpet through a garlanded spandrel, flanked by putti.

title: Hercules and Cerberus
shows: Hercules raises his club and drags the three-headed Cerberus on a chain by the fiery mouth of the underworld.

title: Heracles and Cerberus (bilingual amphora, red-figure side)
shows: Heracles in his lion skin crouches to coax the two-headed Cerberus on a chain beneath a tree.

title: Roman strigilated sarcophagus: Hercules leading Cerberus from the gate of Hades
author: Carole Raddato from FRANKFURT, Germany
shows: A marble relief of Hercules with club and lion skin stepping out of the half-open door of Hades with Cerberus at his feet.

title: Orpheus Interceding with Pluto and Proserpina for Eurydice (drawing)
location: Musée du Louvre, Paris (shown in the 2024 exhibition 'L'incanto di Orfeo', Palazzo Medici-Riccardi, Florence)
author: Francesco Bini
shows: Orpheus kneels with his lyre before enthroned Pluto and Proserpina, Cerberus at their feet, a snake-haired Fury above and bound shades at right.

title: The Rape of Proserpina
author: Alvesgaspar
shows: Marble group of crowned Pluto seizing Proserpina as she pushes against his face, with three-headed Cerberus at his side.

title: The Rape of Proserpina (detail: Pluto's hand)
author: Alvesgaspar
shows: Close-up of Pluto's fingers pressing into Proserpina's marble thigh.

title: Orpheus and Eurydice
shows: Eurydice recoils from the snake's bite at left; at right, by a burning gateway of the underworld, Orpheus leads her and turns back as she slips away.

frames.name: orpheus and eurydice at hell's gate

title: Orpheus before Pluto and Proserpina in the Underworld
artist: Jan Brueghel the Younger (as given on Commons)
shows: Orpheus plays his harp before crowned Pluto and Proserpina in a cavernous, fire-lit underworld teeming with monsters, demons and tormented souls.

title: Orpheus and Eurydice
shows: Orpheus leads Eurydice out of the underworld while Pluto and a dark-veiled Proserpina watch from their throne, Cerberus at their feet.

title: Pluto
author: Sailko
shows: Brooding, bearded Pluto seated on clouds with the key of the underworld, three-headed Cerberus snarling beside him (photographed in its gilt frame).
note: Commons page carries the Italian cultural-heritage (ita-mibac) restriction notice: commercial reproduction of works in Italian state museums may require authorisation.

title: The Rape of Proserpina (Gallery ceiling, Palazzo Medici-Riccardi)
shows: Crowned Pluto carries off Proserpina, arm flung skyward, as her companions cry out among scattered flowers.

title: Persephone and Hades (tondo of an Attic red-figure kylix)
author: Marie-Lan Nguyen (User:Jastrow), 2007
shows: Hades reclines on a banqueting couch holding out a drinking cup while Persephone sits facing him.

title: Red-figure lekythos: Herakles taking leave of Peirithoos in Hades
author: ArchaiOptix
shows: Herakles in his lion skin clasps hands with a seated bearded man in a petasos holding a sceptre, interpreted as Peirithoos left behind in Hades (or Theseus/Admetos being brought out).

title: Relief with Herakles, Theseus and Peirithoos
shows: Marble relief of three heroes: Herakles with his club and the apples, a seated cloaked youth and a standing youth with a staff and sword, the trio linked to Theseus and Peirithoos in the underworld.

title: Odysseus consulting the shade of Tiresias (Lucanian red-figure calyx-krater)
location: Cabinet des médailles, Bibliothèque nationale de France, Paris (De Ridder 422)
shows: Odysseus sits on rocks, sword drawn over the slaughtered ram, as the head of the seer Tiresias rises from the ground, flanked by two companions.

title: Nekyia: Sisyphus in the Underworld (Attic black-figure amphora)
shows: In the underworld, Persephone watches Sisyphus shoulder his boulder while a brooding shade (Ajax) stands behind her.

title: Aeneas and the Cumaean Sibyl in the Underworld
shows: Armoured Aeneas and the Sibyl walk through a ruined, fire-lit underworld of monsters, Death, Sleep and the Elm of False Dreams, beside a glowing river crowded with souls.

title: The Sibyl Showing Aeneas the Underworld (Charon's boat)
shows: A burning infernal city: Charon's ship packed with naked souls, crowds on the shore, demons dragging the damned and a gaping hell-mouth, with a chariot in the smoky sky.

title: Aeneas on the Bank of the River Styx
shows: The Sibyl holds out the golden bough to a scowling Charon in his boat while helmeted Aeneas stands beside her and a naked shade pleads from the bank.

title: Aeneas and the Cumaean Sibyl Entering the Infernal Regions (drawing)
location: The Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York
shows: The Sibyl, bough in hand, leads helmeted Aeneas towards a dark cave where Cerberus waits, a companion with spear and shield behind them and a round temple on the hill.

title: Venus and Psyche (Loggia di Psiche spandrel)
location: Loggia di Psiche, Villa Farnesina, Rome
shows: Psyche, back from the underworld, kneels and gazes up at Venus as she hands over the jar from Proserpina; two doves fly at right.

title: Psyche before Proserpina (lunette, Camera di Amore e Psiche)
artist: Giulio Romano, Rinaldo Mantovano and Benedetto Pagni
location: Camera di Amore e Psiche, Palazzo Te, Mantua
author: Sailko
shows: In the underworld, Proserpina hands Psyche the jar of beauty while white-bearded Pluto, a second old god, a snake-haired Fury, a demon and a wolfish Cerberus crowd around.

title: Story of Cupid and Psyche: Psyche gives honey-cake to Cerberus, visits the Fates and Charon
location: Palazzo Franchetti, Salone degli Dei dell'Olimpo (Hall of Eros and Psyche)
author: Sailko
shows: Psyche kneels to feed a honey-cake to three-headed Cerberus at the underworld gate, with the Fates spinning and Charon's ferry in the distance; framed in painted ceiling ornament.

title: The Wedding Banquet of Cupid and Psyche (Loggia di Psiche vault)
location: Loggia di Psiche, Villa Farnesina, Rome
shows: The gods feast on clouds at a long table for the wedding of Cupid and Psyche: Horae scatter flowers, Graces anoint the couple, Ganymede and putti pour wine, dancers and musicians at left; framed by garlands and painted spandrels.

title: Symposium scene, Tomb of the Diver (side-wall detail)
author: Carole Raddato
shows: Two wreathed banqueters recline on a couch above a low table: one raises a lyre-like object (or plays kottabos), the bearded one holds a shallow wine cup.

title: Funerary plaque (pinax) with prothesis
shows: Attic black-figure plaque of the laying-out of the dead: the body lies on a bier while named mourners, the mother among them, tear their hair and touch the head; men approach at left.

title: Silver obol of Athens (reverse: owl)
author: ArchaiOptix
shows: A tiny (10 mm) Athenian silver obol, the coin placed with the dead for Charon's fare, showing Athena's owl, an olive sprig and the letters ΑΘΕ.
note: Source image is 974 px square; it has been upscaled to 1800 px, so close frames will be soft.

title: The Rape of Proserpina (detail: Proserpina's head)
author: Kent Wang from Barcelona, Spain
shows: Proserpina's marble face tilted back in anguish, lips parted and a tear on her cheek, against the gilded Borghese ceiling.

title: White-ground lekythos: Hermes Psychopompos and a woman at a tomb
author: ArchaiOptix
shows: Hermes as guide of souls, in pilos cap and with his herald's staff, sits on rocks and points the way; the dead woman stands at the edge of this view.
